Best suited to people who are attentive, steady-handed, empathetic, and resilient under pressure. If you can steady a mother through severe pain and still respond calmly to an emergency, this field needs you.

Midwives provide prenatal care, monitor labor and attend births, deliver postpartum and newborn care, educate families about maternal health, and identify high-risk factors for timely referral. They are indispensable professionals in maternal and infant healthcare.

paragraphs: The rhythm of the delivery room is suspenseful waiting: when no one is in labor, midwives prepare delivery kits, organize records, and provide education. Once the cervix is fully dilated, they remain at the bedside, counting contractions, checking the fetal heart rate, and coaching the mother to push. As soon as the baby is born, they assess the Apgar score, manage the umbilical cord, and keep the newborn warm. Attending two or three births in a row on a night shift is routine. By handoff, their legs feel weak, but they leave with a sense of fulfillment.

In one sentence: guide mothers through pregnancy and childbirth and bring new life safely into the world. Duties include prenatal checkups and education, labor monitoring, birth attendance, initial newborn care, postpartum nursing, breastfeeding guidance, and identifying high-risk cases for referral.

subject.summary: Midwives are the first to embrace a new life. From prenatal care and labor preparation to birth attendance and postpartum care, they remain beside mothers throughout the journey and serve as the most compassionate guardians in the delivery room.
